name: braindb-self retrieval gold set
_about: Hand-judged queries over examples/braindb-self/seed.json (no ingest, so the ids are stable).
Two buckets, and the split is the point.
lexical:    the query shares words with the target memory. Any retrieval method should pass these.
paraphrase: the query shares only MEANING. Wording was chosen so that no 5-letter stem of the query
appears in the target text, which is exactly what the offline hash-256 engine indexes.
A lexical engine is expected to fail here; a real embedding model is expected not to.
This gold set asks the questions a maintainer or an agent actually asks about the project,
which is the same reason the sales-company set exists: to measure the thing the brain is for.

SQLite storage engine dependency

embedding cache sha256 model text
MCP tools brain_view brain_run status line

queries.note: target speaks of floors, half-life and knowledge that never leaves the graph; the query speaks of a ruling and a year

queries.q: why does it miss things when I ask in my own phrasing
queries.note: the target says paraphrase, meaning, stems, bigrams, trigrams; none of those words are in the query

queries.q: which library do we lean on so writes survive a crash
queries.note: target says SQLite, write-ahead log, crash safety, one dependency

queries.q: can the assistant lose something I told it
queries.note: target says silently dropping knowledge, invisible and unrecoverable loss, advise versus enforce

queries.q: how much of everything stored does the model read in one turn
queries.note: target says the whole brain is memory, only the lit slice is the working context

queries.q: what stops a repeated run from costing money again
queries.note: target says cached on disk, restarts and re-imports cost no API calls

queries.q: evidence that following connections beats plain similarity
queries.note: target reports graph MRR 1.00 and calls it the measured evidence for the design claim

queries.q: reaching into another team's store of knowledge
queries.note: target says federation, sources, external stubs, remote transports

queries.q: a signpost that adds nothing to the prompt
queries.note: target says connector nodes hold no knowledge, never appear as results and cost no tokens

queries.q: keeping a replaced rule from outranking the current one
queries.note: target gives the weight curve and the 0.3 multiplier for superseded nodes

queries.q: what the assistant should write down before it finishes
queries.note: target is the agent loop: remember the decision, link it to the question, supersede the old rule

queries.q: figures we published that nobody ever checked
queries.note: target says latency and scale are not measured and every such figure is a design target
